determinism.description: The served print PDF is NOT byte-deterministic, which is why L2's comparand was re-cut (rows Z-S254 and the issuer's amendment 3). Control: the SAME request twice, four seconds apart, against the deployed function, with no deploy and no format parameter between them -- so elapsed time is the only variable. Then the rl-10 pin's shape was simulated by rewriting a served body through pypdf with no metadata, which drops /CreationDate AND rebuilds the xref.
determinism.expected: If the renderer were deterministic the two bodies would be identical. If the chosen comparand is sound it must survive BOTH the wall-clock stamp and the pin's entry-removal, while still DIFFERING for a different security.

The /CreationDate-normalised sha did NOT survive the strip (fab9a93f... -> 9895fc74...). Confirmed on the real deploy afterwards: /CreationDate present BEFORE True, AFTER False, 77862 -> 77828 bytes, raw EQUAL False, normalised EQUAL False, content EQUAL True.
